newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: LEIGHTON SEES CONTINUED 2-3 YEAR GROWTH.
newsitem.headline: LEIGHTON SEES CONTINUED 2-3 YEAR GROWTH.

text.p: Leighton Holdings Ltd said on Thursday it expected continued growth over the next two to three years, but could not forecast beyond that period.

"Our own internal analysis shows the company should improve over the next two to three years, past that I really can't tell as you start to get into no man's land," Leighton chief executive Wal King told Reuters.

"The company has a large momentum of work, we have on hand work that will carry through over the next couple of years," he said. He added he expected the group to closely maintain the current level of work in hand, A$4.23 billion, in 1997/98.
Leighton, which is 44.9 percent owned by Hochtief AG, reported a 32 percent rise in net profit before abnormals to A$86.24 million in 1996/97 ended June 30.
At 3.15 p.m. (0515 GMT), Leighton shares up 36 cents or 6.2 percent at A$6.14.
